intended_object: The counit of the composite adjunction (f₁ ≫ f₂) ⊣ (g₂ ≫ g₁) in a bicategory, ε = ε₂ ∘ (g₂ ε₁ f₂) (from the docstring "auxiliary definition for Adjunction.comp" and the type).
explanation: The source (g₂ ≫ g₁) ≫ f₁ ≫ f₂ is reassociated by coherence (⊗≫) to g₂ ≫ (g₁ ≫ f₁) ≫ f₂. Whiskering the counit ε₁ : g₁ ≫ f₁ ⟶ 𝟙 b by g₂ on the left and f₂ on the right gives a 2-cell to g₂ ≫ 𝟙 b ≫ f₂. Coherence then reduces this to g₂ ≫ f₂, and ε₂ maps it to 𝟙 c. This is exactly the standard counit of a composite adjunction, stated for arbitrary bicategories, which is the natural generality. Although the docstring calls it auxiliary, it denotes a genuine mathematical 2-cell, so I classify it as faithful.
